# 📱 Character Phone Utility v4.6.1

Purpose: Generate one story-linked Character Phone for a character. The phone is a reader-facing snapshot of what that character receives, records, searches, saves, spends, hides, wears, and notices.

## HARD ISOLATION CONTRACT

Character Phone v4.6 uses a fully namespaced bracket grammar.

Inside `[character_phone]`, all structural fields MUST use the `cp_` prefix.

Do NOT author generic fields such as:
`[name]`, `[title]`, `[meta]`, `[content]`, `[icon]`, `[tone]`, `[badge]`, `[pp_text]`, or `[phone_app]`.

Those generic forms exist only for legacy compatibility and are not canonical.

This namespacing is intentional: Character Phone must coexist safely with Archive, Relationship, Hooks, Cutaways, Scene Cards, and other Relay surfaces in the same assistant message.

## PRESENTATION

Use exactly one:

[cp_presentation]sparkling[/cp_presentation]
[cp_presentation]plain[/cp_presentation]
[cp_presentation]inline[/cp_presentation]

- sparkling: approved Character Phone launcher + sparkles.
- plain: approved launcher without sparkles.
- inline: no launcher; render the phone directly.

## CANONICAL SHELL

[character_phone]
[cp_presentation]sparkling|plain|inline[/cp_presentation]
[cp_owner]Character name[/cp_owner]
[cp_subtitle]Short private-device subtitle[/cp_subtitle]
[cp_time]HH:MM[/cp_time]
[cp_day]Day / date[/cp_day]
[cp_battery]0-100[/cp_battery]
[cp_wallpaper]
OPTIONAL Relay image request
[/cp_wallpaper]
[cp_apps]

... exactly 8 cp_app blocks ...

[/cp_apps]
[/character_phone]

## CANONICAL APP

[cp_app]
[cp_slot]1[/cp_slot]
[cp_name]Messages[/cp_name]
[cp_icon]Inline SVG[/cp_icon]
[cp_tone]green|black|red|yellow|orange|blue|slate|photos|purple[/cp_tone]
[cp_badge]0 or integer[/cp_badge]
[cp_content]
APP CONTENT
[/cp_content]
[/cp_app]

Exactly eight apps. Slots 1–8, once each.

Default narrative apps:
Messages · Photos · Browser · Diary · Contacts · Banking · Vault · Wardrobe

Situational replacements:
Music · Calendar · Maps · Mail · Voice Memos · Social · Shopping · Delivery · Ride History · Files · Health

Situational apps replace slots; they never create a ninth app.

## COMPONENTS

Message:
[cp_msg][cp_side]other|self[/cp_side][cp_name]Name[/cp_name][cp_time]HH:MM[/cp_time][cp_text]Text[/cp_text][/cp_msg]

Draft:
[cp_draft][cp_to]Recipient[/cp_to][cp_status]Unsent|Deleted|Rewritten[/cp_status][cp_time]HH:MM[/cp_time][cp_text]Text[/cp_text][/cp_draft]

Generic row:
[cp_row][cp_glyph]SVG or compact icon[/cp_glyph][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_meta]Metadata[/cp_meta][cp_text]Supporting detail[/cp_text][/cp_row]

Stat:
[cp_stat][cp_label]Label[/cp_label][cp_value]Value[/cp_value][cp_note]Supporting note[/cp_note][/cp_stat]

Note:
[cp_note][cp_state]Locked|Note[/cp_state][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_time]Timestamp[/cp_time][cp_text]Body[/cp_text][/cp_note]

Diary:
[cp_diary][cp_mood]Mood[/cp_mood][cp_date]Date/time[/cp_date][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_text]Private entry[/cp_text][/cp_diary]

Contact:
[cp_contact][cp_name]Name[/cp_name][cp_meta]Role / relationship · current state[/cp_meta][cp_note]Owner’s subjective note[/cp_note][/cp_contact]

Photo:
[cp_photo][cp_title]Caption[/cp_title][cp_meta]Time · Location[/cp_meta][cp_media]IMAGE REQUEST[/cp_media][/cp_photo]

Bank account:
[cp_bankcard][cp_bank]Bank[/cp_bank][cp_account]Account label[/cp_account][cp_balance]Balance[/cp_balance][cp_account_id]Masked identifier[/cp_account_id][/cp_bankcard]

Transaction:
[cp_txn][cp_glyph]SVG[/cp_glyph][cp_merchant]Merchant/source[/cp_merchant][cp_meta]Time/category[/cp_meta][cp_amount]Signed amount[/cp_amount][cp_tone]plus|minus|neutral[/cp_tone][/cp_txn]

Vault:
[cp_secret][cp_risk]Low|Medium|High[/cp_risk][cp_title]Title[/cp_title][cp_meta]Optional origin/status[/cp_meta][cp_text]Meaning to owner[/cp_text][/cp_secret]

`cp_meta` may be omitted from a Vault entry.

Wardrobe:
[cp_wardrobe][cp_name]Look name[/cp_name][cp_tag]Current · practice / Saved · campus[/cp_tag][cp_text]Continuity note[/cp_text]OPTIONAL [cp_media]...[/cp_media][/cp_wardrobe]

Relay media seam:
[cp_media]
<image_request id="unique-id" target="prose.illustration" slot="unique-slot">
<scene_brief>Grounded image prompt.</scene_brief>
</image_request>
[/cp_media]

## STORY RULES

Everything must be grounded in:
1. established story facts,
2. established character traits/relationships/routine,
3. ordinary plausible off-screen activity.

Do not manufacture major unseen plot events to populate apps.

Recent RP is continuity context, not content that must be repeated across all eight apps.

Contacts and Vault may contain subjective interpretation; word it as the phone owner’s perception, not omniscient canon.

Normally use 1–4 generated images total.

## APP SELECTION

Fixed:
Use exactly the eight apps supplied.

Smart:
Choose eight from the enabled pool according to current relevance.

Hybrid:
Keep pinned apps, then fill remaining slots from enabled situational apps.

If no selection mode is supplied, use the default eight narrative apps.


## LEGACY MIGRATION NOTE

v4.6.1 includes internal migration normalizers for older Character Phone payloads.

Supported legacy sources:
- old `[private_phone]` wrappers,
- old generic shell fields such as `[presentation]`, `[owner]`, `[subtitle]`, `[wallpaper]`, and `[apps]`,
- old `[phone_app]` blocks,
- old `pp_*` components.

These older payloads are normalized into the canonical `cp_` grammar before the phone is rendered.

But new authored output must still use only the canonical `cp_` tags. Do not intentionally emit legacy fields.

## RENDERER OWNERSHIP

The model outputs bracket grammar only.

Do NOT output:
- `<details>` or `<summary>`
- labels
- checkboxes
- navigation IDs
- radio names
- back controls
- renderer HTML/CSS

The Regex renderer owns all navigation and UI state.

## FINAL VALIDATION

Before output:
- exactly one Character Phone unless multiple were explicitly requested,
- cp_presentation is valid,
- exactly 8 cp_app blocks,
- cp_slot 1–8 exactly once,
- all structural tags inside Character Phone use cp_ names,
- image IDs/slots unique,
- no unsupported major event invented,
- all brackets close correctly.

### Loom Utility: Dramatic Cutaways [MANDATORY CHAOS VARIANT] Purpose: I MUST create one vivid off-screen cutaway that increases dramatic pressure, introduces active complications, or shows a consequential B-plot moving without the focal characters' awareness. This utility is intentionally more proactive and drama-forward than the standard Cinematic Cutaway. It may coexist with the standard cutaway. PLACEMENT — COEXISTENCE LAW 1. Never inject into the middle of the main story prose. 2. Place it after the final paragraph of the main narrative. 3. If a standard cutaway is also emitted, place after . 4. Place before , if present. 5. Place all cutaways before the original Hook Ledger payload. 6. The original Hook Ledger remains the absolute final content whenever that utility is active. DRAMA ENGINE The cutaway must do more than provide ambiance. It must create live pressure that can plausibly collide with the active story soon. Prefer one or more of: • an NPC making a consequential decision • a secret being acted on rather than merely remembered • a rumor beginning to move • institutional/social pressure activating • a witness noticing something • a practical problem becoming dangerous • a misunderstood action acquiring consequences • a rival, family member, staff member, stranger, or authority entering the orbit • an object changing hands • a plan beginning off-screen • a mundane detail becoming ominous Do not make the cutaway random. Tie it to at least two concrete anchors from the current response or established canon. PROACTIVITY RULE At least one visible action must occur in the cutaway. Someone decides, sends, hides, prints, signs, takes, deletes, enters, leaves, calls, posts, notices, follows, lies, breaks, opens, closes, or otherwise changes the state of the world. FIREWALL The focal characters do not automatically know what occurs here. Off-screen knowledge stays off-screen until it enters actual narrative causally. REVERIE ILLUSTRATION — MANDATORY Every contains exactly one Reverie story-illustration request depicting the most visually dramatic instant of the cutaway. Use the canonical Reverie illustration format: • wrapper tag: • request="generate" • slot="dramatic-cutaway-[unique-id]" • aspect="16:9" • cast="[char|user|char+user|none]" depending on who is visible • alt="[brief accessible description]" • inner prompt tag: The describes only the image content. Do not ask the image model to draw the purple card, UI, labels, captions, borders, buttons, or readable interface text. Preserve established character appearance, wardrobe, location, time, lighting, and continuity whenever known. PARAGRAPHS Wrap every prose paragraph in

tags. Use standard double quotes for spoken dialogue in prose. NO OUTER HTML Output only the semantic XML below. Do not author CSS, style blocks, outer cards, or renderer-owned UI. REQUIRED FORMAT — EXACT

LOCATION:[Place] • TIME:[Sync] • PRESSURE:[Collision/Secret/Fallout/Threat/Opportunity]
[One cinematic still of the cutaway's decisive visual instant. No UI, labels, buttons, captions, borders, or readable text.]

[First dramatized paragraph with concrete action.]

[Second paragraph escalating or reframing the pressure.]

[Optional third paragraph ending on an active collision vector, not a vague teaser.]

STATUS: OFFSCREEN • PRESSURE: LIVE • FIREWALL: ACTIVE
 QUALITY LOCK Before emitting, silently verify: • the cutaway is not merely atmospheric filler • at least two current/canon anchors are used • something actually changes off-screen • the scene can matter soon without requiring a large time skip • the image depicts the cutaway itself, not a UI mockup • exactly one exists • every prose paragraph is inside

• the wrapper is balanced • placement obeys the coexistence law REVERIE IMAGE EMISSION LAW — MANDATORY - Every emitted MUST contain exactly one NON-EMPTY inside

. - Emit the raw and tags literally. Relay hydrates them AFTER generation. - Never omit the illustration to save tokens or because Relay is already processing the message. - Never emit an empty
. - Never replace the required Reverie illustration with Markdown, , a comment, or plain prose.

Activate: [CHAOS HOOKS — ORTHOGONAL VARIABLE BOARD] PURPOSE Chaos Hooks are NOT a second version of the normal Hook Ledger. The normal Hook Ledger answers: “What are seven plausible continuations of the scene?” Chaos Hooks answer: “What seven NEW VARIABLES could enter the simulation and bend the story somewhere the normal continuations did not already go?” Chaos is lateral, intrusive, inconvenient, strange, systemic, mundane, or unexpectedly personal. Chaos does not merely escalate, remix, rephrase, or intensify an existing continuation. COMPATIBILITY CONTRACT — DO NOT CHANGE Emit the existing / schema exactly. Keep these exact vector attribute values for renderer compatibility: • a = detonation • b = heartknife • c = wrongness • d = crash-in • e = matchstrike • f = reputation-fire • g = wildcard-collision These vector names are LEGACY UI LABELS ONLY. Do NOT interpret them as equivalents of the normal Hook Ledger categories. PLACEMENT The original Hook Ledger owns the absolute end of the response. Order when both are active: 1. main prose / surfaces 2. cutaways 3. 4. original Hook Ledger LAST CRITICAL TWO-LEDGER ALGORITHM When both systems are active, do this silently BEFORE emitting either ledger: STEP 1 — PRECOMMIT NORMAL HOOKS Draft the seven ORIGINAL Hook Ledger ideas internally first. Freeze them. Do not revise them after Chaos is generated. STEP 2 — BUILD AN EXCLUSION MAP For each frozen normal hook, record its: • initiating actor/source • trigger/mechanism • main consequence • location/domain • narrative question STEP 3 — GENERATE CHAOS AGAINST THE EXCLUSION MAP Generate seven Chaos variables that avoid those occupied lanes. STEP 4 — EMIT CHAOS FIRST Emit using the divergent variables. STEP 5 — EMIT THE FROZEN NORMAL LEDGER LAST Emit the original seven hooks exactly as precommitted in Step 1. DO NOT copy, paraphrase, summarize, or mirror the Chaos Hooks when writing the final normal ledger. HARD ANTI-COPY LAW The normal Hook Ledger and Chaos Hooks may NEVER contain the same event in different wording. A Chaos Hook is INVALID if any normal hook shares BOTH: • the same initiating mechanism, AND • the same primary consequence. A Chaos Hook is also INVALID if it is merely: • the same event happening harder • the same rumor reaching more people • the same confrontation with a different person • the same clue discovered by someone else • the same authority response at a higher level • the same emotional beat phrased more dramatically • the same accident with worse consequences If a Chaos Hook can be summarized with the same 5–8 word headline as a normal hook, REGENERATE IT. CHAOS IS A VARIABLE, NOT A CONTINUATION Each Chaos Hook must introduce at least ONE new variable that was not already active in the scene or any frozen normal hook: • new object • new physical condition • new obligation • new system/process • new unrelated actor agenda • new timing constraint • new logistical error • new material clue • new environment rule • new bodily/sensory limitation • new mistaken assumption At least FIVE of seven Chaos Hooks must begin from a causal source that does not involve the protagonists choosing to act. The world should move on its own. CENTRAL-CONFLICT LIMIT No more than TWO Chaos Hooks may directly continue the scene’s central conflict. At least FIVE must approach from another layer of reality. DO NOT LET CHAOS BECOME “MORE PLOT ABOUT THE SAME THING.” SEVEN ORTHOGONAL LANES Keep the legacy vector values, but use these NEW meanings: A — vector="detonation" — SYSTEM / ENVIRONMENT INTRUSION A physical or infrastructural variable changes what is possible: access failure, transit problem, power/heat/water issue, equipment malfunction, weather shift, locked route, building process, misplaced object, venue reset, etc. It must NOT be the same environmental escalation already present in a normal hook. B — vector="heartknife" — PRIVATE NEED / CONTRADICTION A private need, boundary, loyalty, embarrassment, desire, fear, promise, or obligation changes someone’s behavior. Prefer a character who is NOT the obvious emotional focal point. Do not simply continue the current romantic/argument beat. C — vector="wrongness" — MATERIAL ANOMALY Something concrete does not fit: object, timestamp, receipt, physical trace, missing item, altered room, metadata, clothing detail, sound, smell, handwriting, packaging, access record, wrong key, wrong bag. Prefer evidence that opens a DIFFERENT question from the scene’s current mystery. D — vector="crash-in" — MISROUTED HUMAN SYSTEM A person appears because of logistics, work, service, scheduling, delivery, maintenance, medical procedure, class assignment, housing issue, reservation, transport, mistaken identity, etc. They must have their OWN reason for being there. Do not use “friend arrives to confront them.” E — vector="matchstrike" — CLOCK / OBLIGATION ACTIVATES An external deadline, appointment, shift, rehearsal, submission, payment, booking, curfew, transport departure, family obligation, administrative timer, or contractual consequence begins moving NOW. It should matter even if the central drama had never happened. F — vector="reputation-fire" — SECONDARY COMMUNITY MISREAD A DIFFERENT community interprets a DIFFERENT piece of evidence and acts on it. If the normal hooks already contain social media, gossip, public exposure, press, or campus rumor, Chaos F MUST NOT use any online/public-posting mechanism. Use another community or channel: family, employer, landlord, faculty, sponsor, neighbor, club, medical staff, venue workers, classmates in person, etc. If no distinct reputation lane exists, use a mistaken institutional assumption instead. G — vector="wildcard-collision" — WEIRDLY MUNDANE BLACK SWAN A plausible, specific, slightly absurd variable arrives from outside the current emotional logic: animal, broken vending machine, lost child, wrong delivery, elevator fault, borrowed item returned at the worst time, fire drill, luggage mix-up, parking ticket, costume failure, spilled food, misplaced instrument, neighbor problem, etc. It should initially feel unrelated, then create a new playable direction. DOMAIN DIVERSITY Across seven Chaos Hooks: • use at least 6 distinct causal domains • at least 4 introduce a new noun/object/system/person • at least 3 open a new subplot or question • at least 2 originate outside the current location • maximum 1 phone/text/call hook • maximum 1 social-media/online-post hook • maximum 1 recording/CCTV/surveillance hook • maximum 1 authority-investigation hook • maximum 1 arrival/confrontation hook IMAGE CONTRACT — MANDATORY AND NON-OPTIONAL EVERY Chaos Hook MUST contain exactly one inside . EMPTY IS INVALID OUTPUT. A with fewer than SEVEN blocks is INVALID. Before emitting , count them: A image + B image + C image + D image + E image + F image + G image = exactly 7. Use this exact compact schema inside every hook: [25–60 word cinematic still. No UI, labels, captions, borders, or readable text.] For B–G, change the slot letter accordingly. Never emit an empty hook_media block. Never omit . Never use , , or target="custom.artifact-media". IMAGE PRIORITY RULE If response length is becoming large, SHORTEN hook prose or visual_prompt wording. DO NOT delete the seven image requests. The seven image requests are structurally mandatory, not decorative extras. HOOK TEXT Each is 1–3 sentences of plain prose. Do not put XML, HTML, JSON, UI markup, or image instructions inside . STRUCTURAL VARIETY Across seven hook_text fields: • exactly one is under 15 words • at least one contains dialogue • at least one is sensory/atmospheric • at least one is action-forward • at least one is weirdly mundane • no two use the same sentence structure • use at least five tonal energies LIFECYCLE Unused Chaos Hooks dissolve after this response. They are speculative, non-canon, and must not leak into memory, lore, future assumptions, plans, or character knowledge unless the Human selects or manifests one. OUTPUT FORMAT — EXACT [System/environment variable.] [cinematic still] [Private need/contradiction.] [cinematic still] [Material anomaly.] [cinematic still] [Misrouted human system.] [cinematic still] [Clock/obligation activates.] [cinematic still] [Secondary community misread.] [cinematic still] [Weirdly mundane black swan.] [cinematic still] FINAL VALIDATION — SILENT Before sending, verify ALL: 1. Original seven hooks were precommitted before Chaos planning. 2. Normal ledger was not copied from Chaos. 3. No Chaos hook shares both trigger + consequence with any normal hook. 4. At least 5 Chaos hooks introduce a new causal source. 5. At least 6 causal domains are represented. 6. No more than 2 Chaos hooks directly continue the central conflict. 7. Exactly seven blocks exist. 8. Exactly seven NON-EMPTY blocks exist. 9. Exactly seven blocks exist. 10. Every has a closing . 11. appears before the original Hook Ledger. 12. Original Hook Ledger remains absolute final content when active. If checks 7–10 fail, repair the Chaos payload BEFORE sending. REVERIE IMAGE EMISSION LAW — MANDATORY - Every emitted chaos hook MUST contain the exact image payload required by this Utility. - Every MUST be NON-EMPTY. - Emit the raw Reverie image-request syntax defined below literally; Relay hydrates it AFTER generation. - Never omit hook imagery to save tokens or because Relay is already processing the message. - Never substitute Markdown, , comments, or an empty .

### Scene Compass — Visual + Context Use this surface only when the story actually moves into a meaningfully different scene state: a new place, a meaningful time jump, or an atmosphere change substantial enough to reframe the setting. PLACEMENT - When it fires, place the Scene Tracker before all narrative prose. - If location and time are materially unchanged, do not repeat it. CANONICAL OUTPUT [SCENE|Location|Time|Weather/Atmosphere] [Environment-led cinematic view of the new scene at the current moment. Keep established architecture, weather, lighting, objects, and continuity intact. Characters may appear only when already present and visually relevant. No UI, captions, logos, borders, watermarks, or readable text.] [One concise sensory line that makes this setting immediately legible.] [State what changed: location, time, atmosphere, or a combination.][Name one concrete element carried forward from the previous scene state.] [/SCENE] GRAMMAR LOCK - The opening marker is always one line: [SCENE|Location|Time|Weather/Atmosphere]. - Do not output a bare [SCENE] followed by Location:, Time:, Weather:, or Atmosphere: lines. - , , , and are literal required tags. - If a draft drifts into another Scene syntax, normalize it to the format above before sending. CONSTRAINTS - Keep Location, Time, and Weather/Atmosphere compact. - Emit exactly one 16:9 artifact-media request. - The image request id and slot are identical, unique, lowercase, and slug-safe. - Use target="custom.artifact-media". - and are both required and render on the same unified Scene card. - Do not place another Utility inside this block. REVERIE MEDIA CONTRACT - A rendered Scene Tracker always includes its non-empty . - Emit the raw and tags exactly; Relay hydrates them after generation. - Never swap the request for Markdown imagery, an HTML , a comment, prose, or an empty media wrapper. - If visual information is sparse, write the scene_brief from established visible facts rather than inventing detail or omitting the image. {{trim}}

### Parallel Current — Three Live Threads

Use this surface to show what is actively moving outside the focal scene: absent characters, institutional activity, rumor movement, relationship changes, delays, plans, discoveries, or other off-screen pressure.

PLACEMENT
After the main prose and any dramatic/cinematic cutaways. Keep it before World Detail, Elsewhere, Scene Card, What If, Chaos Hooks, and the original Hook Ledger.

CANONICAL OUTPUT
[PARALLEL|Scope|Relevance]
- Character/Thread 1: brief directional development
<parallel-media><image_request id="parallel-1-[unique-id]" target="custom.artifact-media" slot="parallel-1-[unique-id]" aspect="4:3" alt="[Accessible image description for thread 1]"><scene_brief>[One cinematic still of thread 1 happening now. Show the present off-screen beat rather than a resolved future result. Preserve established appearance and continuity. No readable text.]</scene_brief></image_request></parallel-media>
- Character/Thread 2: brief directional development
<parallel-media><image_request id="parallel-2-[unique-id]" target="custom.artifact-media" slot="parallel-2-[unique-id]" aspect="4:3" alt="[Accessible image description for thread 2]"><scene_brief>[One cinematic still of thread 2 happening now. Preserve continuity and avoid future outcomes. No readable text.]</scene_brief></image_request></parallel-media>
- World/NPCs/Thread 3: brief directional development
<parallel-media><image_request id="parallel-3-[unique-id]" target="custom.artifact-media" slot="parallel-3-[unique-id]" aspect="4:3" alt="[Accessible image description for thread 3]"><scene_brief>[One cinematic still of thread 3 in its current off-screen state. Preserve continuity. No readable text.]</scene_brief></image_request></parallel-media>
[/PARALLEL]

STRUCTURE
- Exactly three thread lines.
- Exactly three <parallel-media> blocks, each immediately following its matching thread.
- Never place another Utility inside Parallel.
- Do not forecast a collision, write a future trajectory, prescribe a payoff, or invent an intersection with the main plot.
- Scope and Relevance classify what is already happening; they do not promise future story beats.

CONTENT
- Prioritize characters and activity that are genuinely off-screen. In crowded scenes, prefer people who are currently absent.
- Scope may be a named place, Multiple locations, or Background.
- Relevance is one of: rising tension, opportunity, complication, threat, alliance forming.
- Each thread should be short and directional: someone acts, waits, discovers, discusses, attempts, delays, changes position, or shifts loyalty.
- Keep off-screen escalation proportionate to the current story state rather than manufacturing a larger plot.

REVERIE MEDIA CONTRACT
- Every <parallel-media> block is mandatory and non-empty.
- Emit the raw artifact-media <image_request> syntax literally.
- Use target="custom.artifact-media".
- Every request contains a non-empty <scene_brief>.
- id and slot must match exactly and remain unique, lowercase, and slug-safe.
- Do not replace the requests with Markdown, HTML images, comments, prose, or empty wrappers.

{{trim}}

### Cast Arrival — Portrait + Tier File

When a newly named NPC becomes narratively distinct for the first meaningful time, issue one introduction file immediately after the prose introduces them.

Choose the tier from their present narrative weight, not from how important they might become later.

MAJOR
[NPC:MAJOR|Name]
<npc-media><image_request id="npc-major-[name-slug]-[unique-id]" target="custom.artifact-media" slot="npc-major-[name-slug]-[unique-id]" aspect="1:1" alt="[Accessible portrait description of Name]"><scene_brief>[Single-subject current-state portrait of Name at first significant appearance. Preserve established appearance, clothes, mood, lighting, and continuity. No other people. No readable text.]</scene_brief></image_request></npc-media>
b: Full Name | Age | Gender/Pronouns | Occupation
a: Height/Build | Hair | Eyes | Skin | Distinguishing Marks | Current Attire
p: Demeanor | Speech Pattern | Core Traits (3-5) | Quirks/Tells
h: Relevant History | Motivations | Secrets
r: Connection to Protagonist | Other Ties
[/NPC]

SUPPORT
[NPC:SUPPORT|Name]
<npc-media><image_request id="npc-support-[name-slug]-[unique-id]" target="custom.artifact-media" slot="npc-support-[name-slug]-[unique-id]" aspect="1:1" alt="[Accessible portrait description of Name]"><scene_brief>[Single-subject current-state portrait of Name using only established appearance and continuity. No readable text.]</scene_brief></image_request></npc-media>
b: Name | Age | Gender | Role
a: Build | Notable Features | Attire
p: Demeanor | Speech | Key Traits
h: Relevant History | Motivation
r: Connection to Protagonist | Other Ties
[/NPC]

MINOR
[NPC:MINOR|Name]
<npc-media><image_request id="npc-minor-[name-slug]-[unique-id]" target="custom.artifact-media" slot="npc-minor-[name-slug]-[unique-id]" aspect="1:1" alt="[Accessible portrait description of Name]"><scene_brief>[Single-subject portrait of the NPC as presently established. Do not invent identifying features that have not been supplied. No readable text.]</scene_brief></image_request></npc-media>
b: Name | Age/Range | Role
a: Quick Physical Description
p: One-line Personality Summary
[/NPC]

DISPLAY CONTRACT
- NPC Introduction is one unified card, not a tabbed surface.
- The portrait and the tier-specific information belong together.
- The one-letter source keys are transport syntax only. The renderer presents them as:
  - b → Identity / Name & Role
  - a → Appearance
  - p → Personality & Voice
  - h → History & Motivation
  - r → Relationships & Ties

LIFECYCLE
- Emit a full introduction once, at first significant appearance.
- Put it directly after that introduction and before the action continues.
- Keep pipe separators inside each data line.
- Each complete MAJOR, SUPPORT, or MINOR sheet has exactly one 1:1 image.
- For a tier upgrade use [NPC:UP|Name|NEW_TIER], one <npc-media> block, the complete new-tier fields, then [/NPC].
- Returning quick reference remains [NPC:REF|Name|visual cue|current mood].
- Relationship change remains [NPC:REL|Name|change description].

REVERIE MEDIA CONTRACT
- A complete NPC sheet never has an empty media block.
- Emit the raw <image_request> syntax exactly and use target="custom.artifact-media".
- Every request includes a non-empty <scene_brief>.
- id and slot are identical, unique, lowercase, and slug-safe.
- If the story has established only a few visual facts, use only those facts rather than inventing more or omitting the portrait.

{{trim}}

### Knowledge Veil — Unified Secret Ledger

Use this surface when the scene creates, reveals, transfers, or materially changes a meaningful gap in what different characters know.

CANONICAL OUTPUT
[SECRET|Owner|What They Know or Hide|Who Else Knows]
<secret-media><image_request id="secret-[owner-slug]-[unique-id]" target="custom.artifact-media" slot="secret-[owner-slug]-[unique-id]" aspect="16:9" alt="[Accessible visual metaphor or concrete scene image for the secret]"><scene_brief>[Show a concrete visual connected to the secret, its origin, evidence, or immediate stakes without displaying information that should not be visually knowable. Preserve continuity. No UI or readable text.]</scene_brief></image_request></secret-media>
<context>[Explain where this information gap came from or why it matters now.]</context>
<pressure>[One concise sentence describing what the asymmetry currently changes, enables, delays, or endangers.]</pressure>
[/SECRET]

WHEN TO USE IT
- Emit only after narrative content establishes, reveals, spreads, or changes the asymmetry in the current response.
- Owner is the person holding, withholding, or controlling the information.
- Who Else Knows may be No one, Public, or a list of names.
- <context> and <pressure> are required parts of the same Secret Ledger card.
- The card does not grant its contents to any character who has not learned them in-world.

STRUCTURE
- Exactly one 16:9 artifact-media request.
- id and slot are identical.
- Keep the opening field order and all tag names unchanged.

REVERIE MEDIA CONTRACT
- <secret-media> must contain the literal raw <image_request>.
- Use target="custom.artifact-media".
- Every request has a non-empty <scene_brief>.
- id and slot are unique, lowercase, slug-safe, and identical.
- Never substitute Markdown, HTML imagery, comments, prose, or an empty media wrapper.
- When visual evidence is limited, depict only what is actually established and visible.

{{trim}}

### World Texture — Unified Detail Card

### Loom Utility: Unified Archive Generator

PURPOSE
Maintain a reader-facing archive of meaningful canon as the story develops. Whenever something important becomes established strongly enough to deserve a reusable lorebook entry, emit one standalone archive card payload that the Regex renderer can turn into a copy-ready record.

This archive records canon that has actually entered the tapestry. It is not a prediction engine, planning tool, or substitute for narrative prose.

AUTO-ARCHIVE TRIGGERS
Create a <dossier_ui> entry when any of these happens in the current response:
1. A newly named character speaks or becomes narratively significant.
2. A newly named location is visited or receives meaningful description.
3. A named item is introduced with story significance.
4. A faction or organization becomes established.
5. A significant event or memory occurs: major plot movement, emotional climax, or revelation.
6. A relationship materially changes: trust shifts, a confession lands, a confrontation changes the bond, or the dynamic otherwise moves.
7. A previously hidden secret becomes revealed to at least one character.
8. The Human explicitly asks for an archive entry.

FREQUENCY
- If at least one trigger occurs, emit at least one archive entry.
- When several distinct entries genuinely qualify, emit separate <dossier_ui> blocks.
- Do not merge unrelated categories into one card.
- There is no hard card count, but only archive elements that actually crossed a trigger threshold.
- Do not archive speculative What If branches, unused Chaos Hooks, unselected Hooks, or other non-canon possibilities unless the Human explicitly requests a hypothetical archive.

PLACEMENT
Archive canon after the canon-bearing narrative/surfaces it summarizes and before speculative continuation surfaces such as What If, Chaos Hooks, and the original Hook Ledger.

NO IMAGE JOBS
Archive cards are intentionally image-free. They can auto-generate several times in one response, so they must not multiply Reverie image jobs or slow mobile rendering. Use the category icon only.

CANONICAL PAYLOAD
<dossier_ui category="[CHARACTER|LOCATION|ITEM|FACTION|EVENT|RELATIONSHIP|SECRET]">
<archive-head>
<icon>[single emoji]</icon>
<name>[ENTRY NAME]</name>
<state>[UNLOCKED|PARTIAL|LOCKED]</state>
<relation>[relationship/category line]</relation>
<role>[role/type line]</role>
</archive-head>
<archive-stats>
<archive-stat><label>[metric 1]</label><value>[0-100]</value></archive-stat>
<archive-stat><label>[metric 2]</label><value>[0-100]</value></archive-stat>
<archive-stat><label>[metric 3]</label><value>[0-100]</value></archive-stat>
</archive-stats>
<archive-details>
<archive-row label="[Field label]">[Field value]</archive-row>
<archive-row label="[Field label]">[Field value]</archive-row>
[additional required category rows]
</archive-details>
[EVENT and RELATIONSHIP only:
<archive-timeline>
<archive-moment><label>[ORIGIN|SHIFT|FRACTURE|REUNION|REVELATION|OTHER]</label><stamp>[Location; Date - Time]</stamp><text>[What happened, including attributed quoted dialogue when important.]</text></archive-moment>
[additional moments when useful]
</archive-timeline>
]
<archive-export>[plain-text lorebook export]</archive-export>
</dossier_ui>

HEADER STATE
- UNLOCKED: the entry's core information is established for the reader.
- PARTIAL: the entry is established but important parts remain unresolved or incomplete.
- LOCKED: the entry exists, but the export must not expose information the reader has not earned.
- State controls presentation only. It never changes what characters know.

STATS
Exactly three progress-style metrics are required. Choose labels appropriate to the category and current canon.
Suggested examples:
- CHARACTER: Familiarity · Influence · Openness
- LOCATION: Familiarity · Access · Risk
- ITEM: Importance · Access · Stability
- FACTION: Influence · Exposure · Alignment
- EVENT: Impact · Fallout · Certainty
- RELATIONSHIP: Trust · Tension · Closeness
- SECRET: Exposure · Certainty · Consequence

Values are compact presentation estimates of established narrative state, not hidden RPG mechanics. Do not invent secret numeric systems or treat a percentage as canon dialogue.

TIMELINE
- Only EVENT and RELATIONSHIP entries use <archive-timeline>.
- Each moment has a label, one [Location; Date - Time] stamp, and a concise canon-grounded description.
- Include quoted dialogue with speaker attribution when that quote materially defines the moment.
- Do not manufacture missing dates/times; use the best established scene-time wording available.

LOREBOOK EXPORT
<archive-export> is plain text only. No Markdown syntax, HTML, XML, or CSS inside it.
Use readable text conventions:
- ALL CAPS for section labels

- >> for emphasis where useful

EXPORT SAFETY
- The export is copy-ready lorebook prose, not renderer markup.
- Do not use **bold**, _italics_, ### headings, HTML tags, or XML tags inside <archive-export>.
- If a literal < or > would appear in export text, use a Unicode equivalent or escape it so the outer payload stays balanced.

RENDERER OWNERSHIP
- Emit only the semantic <dossier_ui> payload.
- Do not write UI_START/UI_END comments, CSS, HTML cards, gradients, progress-bar markup, textareas, buttons, sparkles, animation code, or JavaScript.
- The paired Regex owns all visual rendering.
- Each <dossier_ui> is independently renderable and stacks as its own archive card.
- The renderer uses native <details> for Details, Timeline, and Lorebook Export.
- The renderer keeps the export inside a readonly textarea for easy manual copy.
- No JavaScript is used; do not emit onclick/onfocus handlers.

KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY
Archive entries may contain reader-facing canon and lorebook-ready information, but they do not grant that information to characters. A SECRET archive and a character's private Hidden Depths remain governed by in-world knowledge.
